chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Rabie, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

My father said to me: 'O my son! There is nothing that delights the eyes of your father more than swallowing a draught of anger, the consequence of which is patience, and there is nothing that brings me joy if I possess it, even if it costs the humility of my soul, like the red camels.'

key_terms.بِذُلِّ نَفْسِي: with the humility of my soul

ai.seo_question: What is the most pleasing act to a father according to Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) emphasizes that the spiritual satisfaction of a father is deeply rooted in witnessing his child's mastery over their ego through patience (sabr) during moments of anger. He further illustrates the value of humility by stating that even great wealth (red camels) is not pleasing to him if it requires the humiliation of one's soul. This teaching highlights the Shia emphasis on internal character refinement over external status, linking emotional control to familial spiritual joy.
